memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he is to take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting. He is to cast lots for the two goats — one lot for the LORD and the other for the scapegoat. Aaron shall bring the goat whose lot falls to the LORD and sacrifice it for a sin offering." - Lev 16:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two goats, identical, standing side by side. Lots are cast, and their destinies divide. One will die. One will be driven away.

Why two? Because one animal could not picture everything that needed to happen.

Sin has to be paid for — a life given, blood shed, justice satisfied. That is the first goat. But sin also has to be taken away — removed, carried off, gone from the people entirely. That is the second.

Two goats, one atonement. Together they show what a single sacrifice could not.

And then Jesus came, and did both. He died — the wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23) — and He also carried our sin away. John the Baptist saw Him coming and said: Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29). Not merely pays for. Takes away.

Notice too that the lots were cast. The choice was God's, not Aaron's. No human hand decided which goat would die.

Nor did any human hand decide at the cross. This man was handed over to you by God's deliberate plan and foreknowledge (Acts 2:23). Your salvation was not an accident. It was chosen.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of forgiveness mainly as debt paid, or sin removed? Both are true.
2. What does it mean that God chose the way of salvation, not us?
3. Which of these two pictures do you most need today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ my sin was both fully paid for and completely carried away. Thank You that this was Your deliberate plan and not an accident. Amen.
